title: The joy of Eid al-Adha
intro: Four blessed days of Hajj, qurbani and the takbirs.

learn.html: Eid al-Adha is four blessed days – the 10th, 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhul-Hijjah. In these days Muslims do the rites of Hajj, the qurbani and the takbirs of tashriq, hoping for Allah’s mercy and reward. Muslims who can afford it travel to Makkah before Eid for Hajj, the fifth pillar of Islam – so this Eid is also called the Eid of Hajj.
On the day before Eid and on all four days of Eid we recite the takbirs of tashriq, glorifying Allah:

learn.label: Takbirs of tashriq
learn.ar: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ
learn.tr: Allaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar, laa ilaaha illallaahu wallaahu akbar, Allaahu akbar wa lillaahil-hamd!
learn.en: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise!

learn.html: On the morning of the first day we go to the masjid for the Eid prayer. After it, those who can afford it offer a qurbani: a camel or a cow for up to seven people, or a sheep for one person.

items.label: One third of the meat we may keep
One third we give to the poor
One third we give to relatives, neighbours and friends
